title: Proverbs Bible Quiz - Chapter 27
description: Ten questions on Proverbs 27: boasting about tomorrow, the wounds of a friend, iron sharpening iron, and knowing the state of your flocks.

questions.text: What does the first verse say you should not boast about?
questions.explanation: The verse says not to boast about tomorrow, for you don't know what a day may bring.

questions.text: Who should praise you, according to this saying?
questions.explanation: The verse says to let another man praise you, and not your own mouth; a stranger, and not your own lips.

answers.text: Another man, and not your own mouth
Your own mouth and your own lips
No one should ever praise you

questions.text: According to this chapter, what is better than hidden love?
questions.explanation: The saying is: better is open rebuke than hidden love.

questions.text: Whose wounds does this chapter call faithful?
questions.explanation: The wounds of a friend are faithful, although the kisses of an enemy are profuse.

questions.text: What does this chapter say is better than a distant brother?
questions.explanation: The verse says that a neighbor who is near is better than a distant brother.

questions.text: What is a contentious wife compared to in this chapter?
questions.explanation: The verse says a continual dropping on a rainy day and a contentious wife are alike.

answers.text: A heavy stone and a burden of sand
A bird that wanders from her nest
A continual dropping on a rainy day

questions.text: How does the saying about iron continue: "Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens..."?
questions.explanation: The full saying is: iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend's countenance.

questions.text: What will the person who tends the fig tree do?
questions.explanation: The verse says that whoever tends the fig tree shall eat its fruit, just as he who looks after his master shall be honored.

questions.text: The crucible is for silver and the furnace for gold, but by what is a man refined?
questions.explanation: The verse says the crucible is for silver and the furnace for gold, but man is refined by his praise.

questions.text: Why should you know well the state of your flocks, according to this chapter?
questions.explanation: The text says to know the state of your flocks and pay attention to your herds, for riches are not forever, nor does the crown endure to all generations.

answers.text: For a thief may come by night
For the king will demand a share
